# BD1 — Context & Constraints Brief

**Solution:** KSE Memory SDK v3 — Universal Hybrid Knowledge Substrate (SOL-01) · **Client/owner:** Open-source (maintainer: Dale Parr; EY-sanctioned personal OSS project)
**Scope:** Remediate v2.0.0 into a credible, CPU-first, universal hybrid retrieval substrate: honest claims, RRF fusion, user-defined conceptual dimensions, real benchmarks, tiered graph backends.

## Trigger

> When a developer building search over attribute-rich data finds that pure vector retrieval can't answer graded, multi-attribute queries, they need a pip-installable hybrid substrate that fuses embeddings, graph and governed conceptual dimensions locally — fast, with explainable results they can trust.

**Job types:** search/rag, extract · **Human role:** assist, fully automated

## Personas

| Persona | Role | Need |
|---|---|---|
| App developer | Builds retrieval for attribute-rich domains (e-commerce, docs, finance) | Hybrid search that beats pure vectors on graded multi-attribute queries, installable in one command on CPU |
| Sceptical evaluator | Researcher / HN reader assessing claims | Every published number reproducible with one command on documented CPU hardware |
| Platform integrator | Wires KSE into an existing stack (LangChain, agent platforms, graph DBs) | Stable interfaces, tiered backend conformance, connector points for Rainbird/Alphient-class platforms |
| Solo maintainer | Owns the project end-to-end | Automation-heavy ops, scoped support policy, sustainable triage |

## Success Criteria

- **Time:** Quickstart-to-first-hybrid-result < 60s in a fresh venv, CPU-only, no external services or API key; incremental upserts with zero reindex downtime.
- **Quality:** Reproducible nDCG@10 lift over BM25+dense RRF baseline on attribute-heavy slices of BEIR subsets and Amazon ESCI; losses published alongside wins.
- **Adoption:** GitHub star and PyPI download growth post-launch; >=3 external contributors; median issue first-response < 72h sustained solo.

## Current-state metrics

- **~21k** — LOC existing scaffold (v2.0.0)
- **11** — Backend integrations already scaffolded
- **0** — Validated benchmark claims today — by design; Phase 2 generates the real ones

## Constraints (non-negotiables)

### SLO / SLA
- p95 latency: < 150ms in-process hybrid query, 100k-item corpus, CPU-only, local backends (⚠ inferred — confirm during build)
- Throughput: CPU embedding >= 500 items/min single-core via ONNX int8
- Uptime: — (library; CI green per release is the equivalent)
- Ingestion: Real-time per-item incremental upsert; batch rebuild only on schema/model semver bump

### Budget
- Per-task: $0 infra on default path (CPU-only, local)
- Notes: Optional LLM dimension-scoring spend user-borne and opt-in. CI benchmarks CPU-only on GitHub-hosted runners (reduced BEIR subsets); no GPU budget.

### Risk register
Active categories: **IP**, **Brand**. Privacy/PII, Safety, Regulatory: not applicable (in-process library; no user data leaves the machine by default — GOV-02).

IP: EY sanction granted for OSS operation — obtain written record before launch push. Brand: prior simulated benchmark claims (+27%, p<0.001 from time.sleep() harness) must be retracted before any release; credibility is the scarcest asset. MIT licence. Telemetry opt-in only; zero network calls by default.

## The Rule

> **Ship the smallest honest thing: zero-dependency CPU-only local install, RRF fusion, user-defined dimension schema, benchmarked on public datasets with published losses — before any launch, paper, or promotion.**
